answer: Chronological thread anchoring. Each identity must post to a public thread on a fixed cadence; the anchor commits to the prior message hash, forming an unbroken chain. A late or missing post breaks the chain, discarding accumulated position at that vertex. To sustain N identities, an attacker must author distinct, contextually coherent entries across every interval, paying continuous human-time cost per identity—roughly hours weekly each—and cannot batch production onto one mesa without visible timing correlation.
